summary: Tethys/Django app for visualizing NGIAB hydrological model runs. This branch replaces a DB-backed ModelRun registry with a storage-backed one (directory/bucket == registry, described by a manifest.json) and adds browser-driven upload of run archives (presigned S3 PUT or direct POST, followed by out-of-process extract/convert/publish). It also gates run deletion and upload behind new Django permissions (delete_model_runs, upload_model_runs) instead of 'any signed-in user'. Headless/agent parity is partially preserved: adding a run has a scriptable primitive (ingest_archive --archive, and the lower-level ingest.publish()), listing is open over HTTP (getModelRuns), but deleting a run has no non-HTTP primitive, and the new headless add-a-run path plus the upload job's polling schema are both undocumented, which functionally hides them from a non-browser caller who would otherwise have to read source.

capability_map.agent_tool: createUpload + startUpload/uploadRun HTTP endpoints (controllers.py:283-415); headless equivalent: `tethys manage ingest_archive --archive <path> --name <name>` (management/commands/ingest_archive.py:4) or ingest.publish() directly

capability_map.agent_tool: removeModelRun HTTP endpoint only (controllers.py:248-280); NO management command replaces the old `register_run --remove`
capability_map.status: partial-gap: reachable via authenticated+permissioned HTTP POST, but no scripted/CLI primitive exists

capability_map.agent_tool: getModelRuns (controllers.py:242-245), open GET, no auth required

View catchment/troute/TEEHR time series, geospatial data, choropleth matrix

findings.title: No headless/CLI primitive replaces `register_run --remove`; deletion is HTTP-only
findings.detail: This branch deletes register_run.py entirely (git show base:tethysapp/ngiab/management/commands/register_run.py had --list, --remove, and add-by-path). Its replacements are write_manifest, convert_outputs and ingest_archive for adding a run, but nothing replaces `--remove`. The only way to delete a run now is POST /removeModelRun/, which requires an authenticated Django session, a CSRF token, and the delete_model_runs permission (controllers.py:116-152, 248-280). A script/operator without a browser session must now reproduce Django's login+CSRF dance to do what one CLI invocation used to do. Not an absolute blocker (HTTP is still scriptable) but a real ergonomics/parity regression for the 'headless portal with no browser to hand' scenario the README explicitly calls out for the add-a-run path.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a `remove_run` (or `ingest_archive --remove`) management command that calls run_store.delete(name) directly, mirroring the old register_run --remove ergonomics, or explicitly document the curl/session recipe for scripted deletion if a CLI command is intentionally out of scope.

findings.title: ingest_archive --archive (the headless add-a-run path) is not documented anywhere
findings.detail: management/commands/ingest_archive.py:4 documents `tethys manage ingest_archive --archive /path/to/run.tar.gz --name <run-name>` in its own docstring as the intended shell-based counterpart to the browser upload ('an operator with the archive already on the machine should not have to round-trip it through the bucket'). README.md's 'Visualizer Directory Organization' section (lines 42-96) documents write_manifest and convert_outputs for a manually-copied directory, and separately alludes to browser upload needing an account (line 81), but never mentions ingest_archive or that it accepts a local archive. A reader following only the README has no way to discover this command exists, so the one documented headless path for adding a new run is 'copy a directory and run write_manifest', which loses the archive-extraction/name-validation/rejection behavior ingest_archive provides.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a short README subsection under 'Visualizer Directory Organization' documenting `tethys manage ingest_archive --archive <path> --name <name>` as the headless equivalent of the browser upload, including its validation and rejection behavior.

findings.title: README understates the new permission requirements for delete/upload
findings.detail: README.md:78 says 'Only a signed-in user can [delete]' and line 81 says 'deleting a run or uploading one needs an account.' Both read as if authentication alone gates these actions. In this branch, controllers.py:96-152 and app.py:39-46 gate delete/upload behind the delete_model_runs/upload_model_runs permissions (granted via the run_managers PermissionGroup), which is stricter than 'signed in' -- test_delete_permission.py explicitly covers a signed-in-but-unpermitted user getting 403. A script author relying on the README would expect any authenticated session to succeed and be surprised by a 403.
findings.suggested_fix: Update README.md to state that deleting/uploading requires both sign-in and membership in the run_managers permission group (or superuser), and mention where an administrator grants it.

findings.title: Upload job status schema (state/stage/message/run/terminal) is undocumented
findings.detail: createUpload/startUpload/uploadRun/uploadStatus form a small state machine (PENDING/RUNNING/DONE/FAILED, TERMINAL tuple in ingest.py:41-46; terminal flag computed in controllers.py:428) that a script must poll to know when a triggered ingest has finished. It is machine-readable (consistent JSON keys), but there is no README or frontend/README.md section describing the three-call upload protocol (createUpload -> transfer -> startUpload/uploadRun -> poll uploadStatus) or its field meanings, unlike getCatchmentTimeSeries and getCatchmentValueMatrix, which get worked examples in frontend/README.md.
findings.suggested_fix: Document the upload protocol and job status JSON shape (state, stage, message, run, terminal) in frontend/README.md or README.md, so a scripted caller can implement the same 3-call + poll flow as the browser.

findings.title: ingest_archive management command's own CLI/process path is untested
findings.detail: tests/test_upload.py exercises ingest.publish() directly through the `archived`/`ingest` fixtures, giving good confidence in the underlying pipeline, but no test invokes the ingest_archive Command itself (its argument parsing, --job vs --archive branching, _staged() tempfile handling, or the write_status/_fail bookkeping around exceptions). The controllers.py:440-463 subprocess launch (_launch, via django-admin) is also untested end-to-end. This is a testing gap rather than a design gap, but it means the headless CLI entry point recommended as the fix for finding #2 above is currently unverified by CI.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a test that invokes `call_command('ingest_archive', archive=..., name=...)` and asserts the run is published and no CommandError is raised for the --archive path, plus a test for the --job path using a staged fixture.

whats_working_well: All new mutating endpoints (createUpload, startUpload, uploadRun, removeModelRun) return a consistent {"error": "..."} JSON shape with meaningful status codes (400/401/403/404/409/500/503), so a scripted caller can branch on status code alone without parsing prose.
Job ids are validated server-side as 32-char hex uuids (controllers.py:432-437) before reaching a storage key or subprocess argument, closing an injection vector a script could otherwise hit.
getModelRuns and all read endpoints remain open (no auth), preserving the 'share a ?model_run_id= link with anyone' property for both humans and scripts.

ingest.publish() is a clean, directly callable primitive (ingest.py:121) independent of the HTTP layer, so a script does not have to go through Django's test client or an HTTP round trip to add a run -- it can import and call it, or use the ingest_archive command.
Permission checks fail closed (controllers.py:63-83) -- a broken permission lookup denies rather than allows, appropriate for destructive actions.
residual_risks: If ingest_archive is fixed to be documented as the headless upload path but its CLI is never exercised by a test (finding #5), a regression in argument parsing could silently break the only documented non-browser add-a-run path.

No headless deletion primitive means operational runbooks/scripts for pruning old runs (e.g., a retention cron job) will need to reimplement Django auth+CSRF, or will be written against removeModelRun without noticing the permission gate, and fail confusingly.
testing_gaps: ingest_archive management command (both --job and --archive branches, and the _fail/_staged helpers) has no direct test coverage.
The subprocess launch path in controllers._launch (django-admin invocation) is not exercised by any test; only the synchronous pieces around it are.
